# coroot: 26 undocumented behaviour changes to diagnose without a test suite

Agents report what they observe about a cluster, this service keeps those measurements, and questions about the services running there are answered from them. Since the last sync of this tree a wide spread of everyday operations returns answers that are subtly or completely wrong, and nothing in the commit history explains any of it. The repository has received 26 separate undocumented edits. Everything below was observed from the outside, written down by what someone was doing at the moment it went wrong.

Start with what arrives from outside and has to be understood. Turning a sampled call-stack line into a display name and a grouping key gives wrong answers when the line is three space-separated pieces — a source path, a symbol and a trailing line marker, or a Java-style return type, signature and line marker. A line that is one package-qualified symbol followed by the line marker still comes back as expected. Asking which of a host's reported addresses should stand for that host hands back the wrong one: given a shuffled mix of loopback, reserved-range and globally routable addresses, the answer contradicts the preference order, so a loopback or routable address comes back although a reserved-range address was offered, and among several reserved-range candidates the one returned is not the expected one. Two independent mistakes are at work there — judging whether an address sits inside a reserve
